newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenia BTC GDR issue six times oversubscribed.
newsitem.headline: Slovenia BTC GDR issue six times oversubscribed.

text.p: Slovenian shopping center operator BTC said on Tuesday it had successfully completed the sale of its debut global depository receipt (GDR) issue last Thursday, raising $22.1 million in fresh capital.
BTC said the offer was six times oversubscribed.

"We started the GDR programme in order to get capital for an even faster pace of development. We want to become the biggest shopping center in the Central European area," Joze Mermal, head of BTC's management board, told a news conference.

He said the company planned to increase its shopping, sport and business center areas in Ljubljana by about 40 percent within the next couple of years from 100,000 square metres (1,076,400 square feet) currently.

BTC sold 2,292,670 GDRs, each representing 10 shares and priced at $9.26. The issue raised BTC's equity by 229,267 new shares to a total of 830,000 shares with a nominal value of 8,000 tolars each. New shares represent 28 percent of the company's total equity.
The issue is the second international offer by a Slovenian company, following a GDR programme launched by bank SKB in February.
BTC said an additional 940,000 GDRs were issued in exchange for 94,000 BTC shares which were held by SKB, one of BTC's five major shareholders. SKB led the GDR issue along with Nomura International.
BTC said its GDRs had started trading over Reuters on Monday, while they were expected to be listed on the SEAQ segment of the London bourse on June 20.
The company said arbitrage between the Ljubljana and London markets would not be possible for at least six months but added it would try to arrange it within a year.
According to international accounting standards, BTC's net profit rose to 625.8 million tolars in 1996 from 483.8 million a year earlier. Sales were up at 3.8 billion tolars from 3.4 billion in 1995.

The Ljubljana bourse suspended BTC's shares on Tuesday morning after they fell 3.29 percent to 14,120 tolars in early trade. Trading is expected to resume on Wednesday. -- Marja Novak, Ljubljana newsroom, 386-61-125-8439
